on_screen_text.text: of the great state of Georgia,
I want people to have more.
One of my earliest political memories
is actually going to vote with my parents.
I'm the second of six kids,
so we look like make way for ducklings
trailing out of the voting booth.
But my parents wanted me to watch them
And that's what I want from you —
because you have the right to more.

spoken_summary: Stacey Abrams introduces herself and announces she is running for governor of Georgia. She says she wants people to have "more"—more money, opportunity, and freedom. She recalls a childhood memory of her parents taking her and her five siblings to vote, comparing them to the story "Make Way for Ducklings." She concludes by asking viewers to make their voices heard because they "have the right to more."
audio_music: An upbeat, rhythmic, and positive instrumental track plays consistently throughout the video, serving as background music for the speech.
editing_pacing: The video consists of a single, static talking-head shot. The main editing feature is the use of animated emojis and graphics that appear and disappear on screen to correspond with the speaker's words.
central_claim: Stacey Abrams is running for governor of Georgia on a platform of providing more economic opportunity and freedom, and she urges people to exercise their right to vote.
intended_effect: To create a positive and relatable image of Stacey Abrams, introduce her campaign message, and encourage voter participation.
